The Gitksan language is spoken in the Skeena Valley, and it is one of the three principal dialects of the Tsimshian language family — along with Nisgha and Coast Tsimshian. Gitksan is distinct from Nisgha and Coast Tsimshian, and the Gitksan people themselves refer to their language as “Sim’algax,” meaning “the real or true language.” The term “Gitx̲lanimx” (or similar) does exist, but it is not commonly used. The Gitksan people also refer to their language as “Amst,” which denotes the more formal variety used in public settings, though this term is less known than Sim’algax. Another term, “Gaanilnx,” is used by some older Gitksan people, but it also includes Nisgha and is a Coast Tsimshian loanword meaning “the interior language.”

records.original_response:
I am not.

(Note: The Gitksan phrase “Nihl g̲abit” is a negative existential construction, literally meaning “There is not [a thing]” or “There is nothing.” In context, it is often used to express “I am not” or “There is no one,” depending on the grammatical context. However, without additional context, the most direct and natural translation in English is “I am not.”)
